analysis.title: Building resilience for 2027 (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: UBS CIO launched its Year Ahead 2027 outlook, 'Sustaining resilience'. The central message is to take risk more deliberately rather than retreat from markets: put excess cash to work, address portfolio concentration, rebalance toward fixed income and add differentiated return drivers.

UBS downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral. It cites elevated expectations, index concentration and uncertainty around the AI investment cycle, which leave less room for disappointment after a multi-year bull run.
Asset class ranking for 2027: most favorable risk-reward in bonds and commodities, followed by equities, with cash the least preferred.

Base case: global growth near trend, further corporate earnings growth, AI infrastructure investment sustained by computing demand, and easing inflation allowing bond yields to decline modestly later in the year.

Risk scenarios: sticky inflation, elevated government debt and geopolitical risks could push bond yields higher and equities lower. A second scenario has AI execution and monetization risks undermining confidence in AI returns across the value chain.

UBS expects global AI-related investment to rise from USD 1.0 trillion in 2026 to USD 1.5 trillion in 2028. Cumulative US technology investment could approach USD 5.0 trillion by 2028, and revenues probably need to reach at least USD 1.5 trillion by 2030 for an adequate return.

AI return threats named: competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models. External financing is getting harder, and market concentration, regulatory and company-specific risks could raise volatility.

The top 10 S&P 500 firms, most of them AI-exposed, make up 39% of the index. UBS says the market may start to apply a lower multiple to future earnings to reflect rising risks, including stickier inflation, higher Fed policy rates and higher bond yields.

Equity positioning: refocus and diversify away from concentrated technology positions. The Eurozone is the preferred equity market, with 15% earnings growth forecast for 2027, comparable to the S&P 500 but from a lower starting valuation. Sector preference is industrials and health care, and US equal-weight strategies can reduce tech concentration.
The equal-weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the market-cap-weighted index by around 7 percentage points since the start of June.

Bonds: elevated starting yields give income and a cushion against rising rates. The best fixed income return opportunity is in emerging market and high yield bonds. UBS favors intermediate duration (maturities of about two to 10 years), with shorter-dated bonds in growth-sensitive credit segments.
US high yield is described as resilient: 60% of the market is rated BB, expected defaults are around 2%, and only 3% of the universe matures over the next year.
Gold upgraded to Attractive. Structural demand and an eventual easing in real yields should support a recovery toward USD 5,000 an ounce by December 2027.
Oil should remain supported in the first half of 2027. Copper is the preferred industrial metal, on demand from electrification, power networks, data centers and AI infrastructure.
Currencies: sterling is the preferred G10 carry opportunity, and select emerging market currencies may benefit from high yields and relatively contained volatility.
Alternatives: favored areas are hedge fund strategies that exploit market dispersion, operationally focused private equity and secondaries, and infrastructure with visible cash flows.
